summary: This note is the README for the Intel RealSense ROS wrapper, which exposes RealSense depth cameras as ROS2 nodes. It covers supported ROS2 distributions and Ubuntu/Windows installation steps, camera naming and namespaces, runtime and launch-time parameters, coordinate conventions, extrinsics, published topics, RGBD and metadata topics, and post-processing filters. The page is cut off partway through the HDR section.
one_line: README for the Intel RealSense ROS2 wrapper covering installation, camera parameters, coordinate frames, published topics and post-processing filters.
key_facts: The Intel RealSense ROS1 Wrapper is no longer supported because the developers focus on the ROS2 distro; the ROS1 wrapper is in the ros1-legacy branch.
In the ros2-development parameters, "stereo_module" and "l500_depth_sensor" are replaced by "depth_module".
The ROS2 wrapper's "filters" parameter is removed; all filters are enabled or disabled using "<filter>.enable".
Supported ROS2 distributions listed for installation are Iron and Humble on Ubuntu 22.04 and Foxy on Ubuntu 20.04.
The wrapper is not meant to be supported on Windows by the RealSense team, since ROS2 is not fully supported over Windows.
The default camera namespace is "camera" and the default camera name is "camera".
The ROS2 coordinate system is X: Forward, Y: Left, Z: Up, while the Camera Optical Coordinate System is X: Right, Y: Down, Z: Forward.
In RealSense cameras, the origin point (0,0,0) is taken from the left IR (infra1) position and named the "camera_link" frame.
For the D435i example, the depth sensor is on the right of the RGB sensor by 0.0148m (1.48cm) in the optical X coordinate.
The extrinsic message contains float64[9] rotation as a column-major 3x3 rotation matrix and float64[3] translation in meters.
The parameter serial_no requires an underscore prefix, for example serial_no:=_831612073525.
The reconnect_timeout parameter sets the retry timeout in seconds when the driver cannot connect to the device.
The unite_imu_method parameter value 0 means none, 1 means copy, and 2 means linear_interpolation.
The default value of tf_publish_rate is 0.0 Hz, which means no dynamic TF is published.
The pointcloud filter is unordered by default and can be set ordered with pointcloud.ordered_pc; pointcloud.allow_no_texture_points colors regions beyond the texture with zeros.
The GPU-accelerated GLSL processing for PointCloud and Colorizer filters requires building with -DBUILD_ACCELERATE_GPU_WITH_GLSL=ON.
